description: This bar chart illustrates the distribution of parameter updates across layers for five different fine-tuning designs: Increasing, Uniform, Decreasing, Spindle, and Bottleneck. The horizontal axis displays the design names as categories, listed alphabetically, while the vertical axis represents the magnitude of parameter updates, labeled as “Parameter Updates,” with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1.2, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Each design is represented by a set of five light green bars, each corresponding to a layer. For the “Increasing” design, the bar heights range from approximately 0.2 to 1.0. The “Uniform” design shows bars of approximately equal height, around 0.6. In the “Decreasing” design, the bar heights range from approximately 1.0 to 0.2. The “Spindle” design features bars that are tallest in the middle two layers, reaching approximately 0.8, and shorter on the outer layers, around 0.3. Finally, the “Bottleneck” design has two taller bars in the center, reaching approximately 0.7, and shorter bars on the ends, around 0.2. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlines, or annotations.
